children: Copper recovered from a three-week low on Tuesday, as lower prices drew physical buyers back in top consumer China, while rising London Metal Exchange inventories and a cash discount pointed to easing near-term supply tightness.
The benchmark three-month copper on the LME
rose 0.55% to $14,078 a metric ton by 0330 GMT, after sinking to $14,018.50 on Monday.
The most-traded copper contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange
fell 0.80% to 107,320 yuan ($15,996.42) a ton, but recovered from an overnight low of 106,650 yuan, its lowest in more than three weeks.

Lower prices encouraged some physical buying in China, with demand showing signs of recovery, traders said, after a selloff triggered by a Reuters' report last week on the White House's hesitation over imposing tariffs on the red metal.
The Yangshan copper premium (SMM-CUYP-CN), a gauge of Chinese demand for imported copper, rose to $100 a ton on Monday, the highest since mid-August.
Meanwhile, signs of improving exchange availability have eased concerns over immediate supply tightness.

Copper stocks in LME-registered warehouses (MCUSTX-TOTAL) jumped 3.59% on Friday to 242,900 tons, while the LME cash contract traded at a discount of as much as $85.75 a ton to the three-month contract (CMCU0-3).
"Rising inventories and softer nearby spreads suggest that the extreme tightness across the LME market is beginning to moderate," ING analysts said in a note.
U.S. COMEX copper stocks (HG-STX-COMEX) were little changed at 767,599 short tons, or about 696,400 metric tons.
ING said copper could remain under pressure in the near term as stretched positioning unwinds, though persistent mine-supply constraints should continue to support prices.
A stronger dollar and caution ahead of the Federal Reserve's policy decision remained headwinds for base metals.
The dollar
hovered near a two-week high on Tuesday as markets increasingly priced in a rate hike.
LME aluminium
rose 0.51%, tin
gained 0.59%, while zinc
fell 0.05%, lead
lost 0.13% and nickel
slipped 0.02%.
SHFE aluminium
rose 0.35%, while zinc
fell 1.53%, lead
dropped 0.91%, nickel
lost 0.77% and tin
declined 2.17%.
($1 = 6.7090 Chinese yuan renminbi)
